maya: Heads-up, APAC-gpu-pool-3 just had a burst of ECC correctables across 4 cards in rack-11. Observed ~120 correctables/min for 10m.
devon: Oof. Any Xid outs or OOMs?
maya: No Xids yet. Just rising correctables + some retries in our job logs. Temperature normal.
ryan: Can you paste the prometheus query? want to see per-card trend.
maya: `sum(rate(nvidia_gpu_ecc_correctable_total{cluster=\"apac\",pool=\"pool-3\"}[5m])) by (card)`
ryan: thx. That looks like a 3x jump on card 11-02 and smaller blips on 11-03/11-04.
sasha: How long before we auto-drain? current policy is 200/min sustained for 5m per-card, and 3 cards in pool within 15m triggers pool soft-evac.
maya: Right. This is below per-card threshold but multi-card pattern is worrying — could indicate PCI bus flakiness.
devon: Maybe we should try a short hysteresis tweak: allow 90s for transient bursts, but if other signals (retry rate, job failures) spike, escalate earlier.
ryan: We should also look at persistent counters: if correctables don't reset after soft-reset, thats bad. Query: `increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1h])`
ops-bot: NOTE: Recent firmware for 40XX cards pushed in apac last week. Could be correlated. See deploy log #apac-fw-2026-03-10.
sasha: Good catch. If firmware changed, we should bias away from immediate pool-wide drains and instead isolate cards showing sustained growth post-fw.
maya: Proposal: implement a \"noisy-card budget\" per rack: allow N correctable bursts per card per hour (e.g., 300) before hard-drain; but if 2+ cards in same PCI domain exceed 150/hour, escalate to soft-drain for rack and schedule maintenance.
devon: Need to add extra enrichment signals: xids, pci-reset-count, nvlink errors, and VM /container restart rate. If these co-occur, lower the auto-drain threshold.
ryan: Also account for job criticality: reserved workloads (dedicated) should not be preemptively drained unless we can migrate with minimal impact. For preemptible jobs, be aggressive.
sasha: I'll sketch playbook steps: 1) annotate noisy-card (mark in metadata), 2) attempt remote pci-rescan and soft-reset, 3) if correctables persist for 30m -> cordon node & migrate non-reserved jobs, 4) if xids or increases after reset -> schedule replace and hard-drain.
maya: Add rollback: if metric rate drops 80% within 15m after reset, unmark and leave in service.
devon: Cost note: draining a node costs ~2h throughput loss while jobs move; migration autoscaling sometimes spins new GPUs -> potential $Xk/day. Add that to the incident runbook so oncall knows to weigh the tradeoff.
ryan: We should add a lightweight alert variant: Warn (pager-silent) on 2 cards >100/hr in rack, Pager on 2 cards >150/hr + retry rate >5% for 10m.
sasha: I'll open a PR with the updated thresholds + playbook. Maya, can you attach the 5m/1h graphs and the node id?
maya: Pushed link: https://grafana.redwood/apac/d/GPUs/stack?var-node=rack-11-node-02 
ops-bot: Deploy planner: PR #3421 created by sasha - auto-drain-hysteresis-playbook. Scheduled review for 3 hours.
ryan: thanks folks. If we see Xids spike, let's escalate to oncall immediately and start sched replace. For now watch and run soft-reset on 11-02. :eyes:
